images.title: One square foot, 144 square inches
images.purpose: Shows a 1 ft square divided into 12 by 12 inch squares, so 1 ft² = 144 in².
images.composition: One large square, centred, with a fine 12 by 12 grid and one small square highlighted.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, lots of empty space, the figure large and centred, thin dark outlines (#2B2B2B), flat fills. Only the labels listed appear; no other text, no scenery, no characters. A large square outlined thick dark, divided by thin grey (#6B7280) lines into 12 columns and 12 rows, 144 small equal squares. The large square is filled very pale teal (#0072B2). The bottom left small square is filled solid amber (#E69F00). Labels: 12 in under the bottom side; 12 in beside the left side; 1 in² with a short pointer to the amber square; 1 ft² = 144 in² to the right of the square. Check: 1 ft = 12 in and 12 × 12 = 144.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A square unit converts by the length factor times itself: 12 × 12 = 144.
images.description: Shows a 1 ft square divided into 12 by 12 inch squares, so 1 ft² = 144 in².
images.context: Practice concept; matches the exercise 'How many in² is 1 ft²?'.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the child to guess 12 or 144 before counting rows.

image_decisions.why: The squared conversion factor is seen by counting a 12 by 12 grid, against the same factor misconception.
